case_name: Bikkar Singh v State of Punjab
respondent:
State of Punjab
Supreme Court of India

20 March 1989
Cr.A. No. 63 of 1983 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 24 February 1982 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Cr.A. No. 688/DB of 1981)
The Judgment was delivered by: RAY, J.
1. facts: This appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment and order made on February 24, 1982 by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana, in Criminal Appeal No.
The prosecution case unfurled in brief is that the deceased, Jagjit Singh, son of Jugraj Singh went on March 29, 1981 at about 6.30 p.m.
Jagjit Singh quarreled with Bikkar Singh that he was selling adulterated liquor.
On hearing about the quarrel Jugraj Singh, father of Jagjit Singh, since deceased, came there.
Both the accused-appellant and his son, Sikandar Singh, were armed with 12 bore guns and one Mukhtiar Singh was also armed with a 12 bore gun.
They surrounded Jagjit Singh.
Sikandar Singh raised a lalkara that Jagjit Singh should not be spared.
Then Bikkar Singh fired one shot from his double-barrel gun which hit the right side chest of Jagjit Singh who tried to run away when another shot was fired from behind.
Jugraj Singh and Mela Singh raised an alarm whereon the accused fled away with their weapons towards the village.
Jugraj Singh left his wife near the dead body of Jagjit Singh and he went to the Police Station, Baghapurana and lodged FIR, Ex. P. K., at about 7.15 p.m.
PW 5, ASI Ram Prakash immediately came to the spot and made an inquest of the dead body of Jagjit Singh (Ex. P. C.).
He picked up two empty cartridges cases (Exs. P. 7 and P. 8) from the spot.
The accused was arrested on April 4, 1981.
Bikkar Singh Made a disclosure statement that he handed over his gun to his brother, Gurdial Singh.
On April 12, 1981 Gurdial Singh, produced the gun in the police station.
The gun and the empty cartridge cases were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory, Chandigarh.
It appears from the report given by the Director of Laboratory that the two cartridges were fired from the gun marked 'A' of the appellant.

PW 1, Dr. B. K. Goyal who conducted autopsy on the dead body of the deceased, Jagjit Singh found three gunshot injuries and he opined that death was due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of the said injuries which were sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature.
He further stated that injury No. 1 was individually sufficient to cause death.
PW 2, Dr. Anoop Sood examined Bikkar Singh, accused on March 29, 1981 and found multiple blisters and swellings and contusions on the left side of chest.
The accused was examined under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he denied prosecution allegations.
Sikandar Singh pleaded alibi.
Accused Bikkar Singh in reply to question No. 16 pleaded as follows:
Jagjit Singh, deceased alone came to my liquor vend.
He quarreled with me and he fired two shots at me while I was standing in the liquor vend and I was injured.
In self-defence I took my licensed gun and fired two shots one after the other at Jagjit Singh and he ran away.
Sikandar Singh and Mukhatiar Singh were not present there nor the PWs.
I was admitted that very evening in the Civil Hospital.
My injuries the doctors, after my bail application was argued and they came to know of my defence.
issues: Whether the accused-appellant fired two shots in self-defence or not?
petitioner_arguments: The accused-appellant pleaded that he fired two shots in self-defence as Jagjit Singh, deceased alone came to his liquor vend and quarreled with him.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution argued that the accused-appellant did not fire two shots in self-defence but instead committed murder of Jagjit Singh.
court_reasoning: As is inevitable in a case of the present kind, the ocular account is the core of the prosecution case.
Jugraj Singh and Mela Singh PWs have given an account thereof which is remarkable in its consistency.

It is borne out from the record that Mela Singh had accompanied the deceased to the liquor vend to the appellant to purchase a bottle of liquor and in the meanwhile Jugraj Singh, PW also reached there.

The circumstances of the lodging of the first information report with promptitude and mentioning therein the names of the appellant and his two associates, the eyewitnesses and the rest of the incriminating circumstances that have been deposed to at the trial by the witnesses lends guarantee to the truthfulness of the version deposed to by the witness.
The medical evidence also lends necessary assurance to the conclusion that it was the appellant who perpetrated the crime.
holding: We dismiss the appeal. Appeal dismissed.
